objective: Price a forecast-free semiconductor theme risk budget for the ETF pilot (S3 0.642 + C2 0.358 per plan v2 D7.1, proposal due 10-15): cap each sleeve's ex-ante theme risk share at 0.40/0.30/0.20/0.10 by substitution (CAP) or theme-neutral hedges (H1 margin, H2 cash), measure the same-volatility recent Sharpe cost and the stress and theme-shock benefit, and select the tightest level within a 0.10 cost as the pilot concentration limit (owner 10-04: remove the overly obvious semiconductor correlation; plan v2 section 3.2 stage 1).
target_regime_and_horizon: US ETF sleeves, daily data 2016-01..2026-10-02 (last archive session). Decision on the recent window 2024-01-08..last session; stress 2017-10-02..2023-08-31 and three SMH shocks (2024-07, 2025-04, 2026-07) measure the benefit. Monthly S3 (5 offsets), calendar-anchored C2. Risk policy, horizon = the pilot's life (reviewed monthly).
existing_solution_comparison: Professional practice manages industry or theme exposure as factor risk with limits and stress tests (MSCI Barra USE4; MSCI thematic stress tests; Roncalli-Weisang factor risk contributions) and adds transient factors when the base model misses a fast theme (Tzikas et al. 2026, Stanford/BlackRock). Nobody publishes the cost of a semiconductor budget on a levered ETF momentum sleeve; our own S3 attribution (H-20260923-09) shows SOXL + USD are 58.5-69.4% of S3's weight and drive its Sharpe, and no local experiment ever capped or hedged the theme (bear guards and defense-first were timing rules, refuted 09-23).
remaining_evidence_gap: (1) The same-volatility recent Sharpe cost of each cap level and version on the pilot; (2) whether caps reduce the three SMH shock losses and stress ES; (3) whether hedges fit Alpaca margin or cash-account rules at the needed size; (4) the theme share of each sleeve's recent P&L (standard 5a: single theme above half); (5) whether a sector placebo cap costs the same (semis-specific dependence).
negative_experiments_checked: Registry and cards: H-20260923-09 s3 attribution (levered semis position; leave-SOXL-out Sharpe 2.28 -> 0.96), H-20260923-11 s3 bear guard (refuted: SMA and credit gates, no gain beyond same-exposure vol target), H-20260923-12 s3 defense first (refuted), H-20260918-01 risk-controlled momentum vs SPMO (refuted), I-20261004-06 (local S3 regime gates all refuted; recommends a theme budget first). None budgeted or hedged theme risk; this stage is a risk policy and cannot refute P2 (owner depth rule 10-04).
cost_and_execution_assumptions: Signal at close d, effective at the open of d+1 (frozen sleeve engines and legs); 10 bp per side on all traded notional (frozen contract), 2x check 20 bp and 100 bp/yr borrow; borrow 0 on easy-to-borrow ETFs (Alpaca 10-04; SMH and SOXX ETB in the 10-01 asset snapshot; live use must check easy_to_borrow daily, fall back to CAP if hard to borrow); debit and same-vol re-levering at 6.5%/yr; Alpaca margin rules for H1 feasibility; H2 funded only from sleeve cash with actual SOXS and UPRO returns.
stop_condition: Measurement of a risk policy: the stage ends when the preregistered outputs exist. Mechanical status: pilot_limit_selected (tightest level within cost and with benefit), cost_ok_no_benefit_monitor_only, or no_level_within_cost (S3 enters the pilot only at pilot size per plan v2 3.2; T-58 carries the theme as one risk unit; the stress-validated theme rule moves to P2 Stage 2). If an identity check fails, stop before computing any capped number.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: Brief T-20261005-32: build TRS, substitution and hedge machinery on the frozen sleeve engines (identity <= 1e-12 for S3 offsets, <= 1e-10 for C2), freeze replay dates in build.json, then evaluate 12 configurations on the pilot plus report-only objects, placebos, 2x cost and feasibility, and write the mechanical status.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: A version has an eligible level if its same-volatility recent excess Sharpe change >= -0.10 and (mean same-vol R1-R3 peak-to-trough return improves >= 1.0 pp or stress same-vol ES97.5 falls >= 5% relative); the tightest eligible level (CAP preferred, then H2F, then H1F unless a hedge is eligible at a strictly tighter level) becomes the pilot limit.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: No level of any version within the 0.10 cost: no sleeve-level cap is adopted automatically; S3 is theme-dependent and enters the pilot only at pilot size; T-58 budgets the theme at the account level. This does not refute P2 or the regime layer.

sources.market_and_period: theory with multi-asset illustrations (equity and bond indices), no specific market period
sources.limitations: Theory; no semiconductor or cost evidence.
sources.independent_replication: Standard result (Euler allocation; also Menchero-Davis x-sigma-rho); not an empirical claim.
sources.claim: Roncalli and Weisang (Risk Parity Portfolios with Risk Factors, MPRA 44017, 2012): the Euler decomposition holds in factor coordinates; Theorem 2 gives the volatility risk contribution of factor j as (A'x)_j (A+ Sigma x)_j / sigma(x); budgets set on assets can leave factor risk unbalanced (7 equity + 3 bond indices -> equity is 70% of ERC risk).
sources.core_claim: if the universe includes 7 equity indices and 3 bond indices, the equity risk of the ERC portfolio represents then 70% of the portfolio’s total risk, a solution very unbalanced between equity and bond risks.
sources.applicability: TRS = Euler contribution of the orthogonalised SMH factor to sleeve variance is the capped quantity.

sources.claim: MSCI Barra USE4 models equity returns with industry and style factors plus specific risk; industry exposure is risk in the factor covariance, not a forecast.
sources.core_claim: using countries, industries, and styles as explanatory factors, as described by Grinold, Rudd, and Stefek
sources.applicability: A theme is managed as a factor risk unit with a budget; motivates the cap rather than cycle timing.

sources.claim: Stanford and BlackRock authors: commercial risk models may miss changing regimes and transient factors; adding transient statistical factors captures the missed structure.
sources.core_claim: while these models are typically of high quality, they may fail to capture important information, e.g., changing market regimes and transient factors.
sources.applicability: Use a dedicated rolling theme factor (126 sessions) rather than a static industry map.

sources.applicability: Benefit is measured with theme-shock replays and stress-window ES, not only full-sample Sharpe.
